text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — High error rate and tail latency for enterprise tenant 'Gallant' in eu-west1. Alerts: 5xx spike (app), connection timeouts to dedicated pool. Automatic warm capacity spin-up in us-east1 started at 2333333020. Paging oncall.

oncall-sre: taking this. joining bridge in 2. creating a private zoom and posting link.

oncall-sre: bridge: https://zoom.company/gallant-2333333000

marta_pm: thx. Gallant account manager on call is @ops:liaison. Customer reports degraded API responsiveness for their internal users — business impact: order ingestion delay. Liaison is looping customer-ops.

ops:liaison: confirmed. Customer-ops-gallant on our bridge, says ~30% of requests returning 5xx and some websocket disconnects. They've already put a rate limiter on their side.

alex_soleng: summary from logs: backend pool serving Gallant in eu-west1 (dedicated-gpu-42) shows increasing OOM/restarts on model workers + long queue latency. Kernel logs show repeated eviction ~2333332980.

kyle_infra: checking node telemetry and GPU metrics. running: `rdwctl pool status dedicated-gpu-42 --region eu-west1` -> degraded, 2/6 nodes NotReady, pod crashloop 2.

sasha_neteng: also seeing a spike in SYN_RECV from the tenant VPC egresses to the model-serving cluster around 2333332955 — suspiciously correlated with a customer traffic spike.

oncall-sre: action plan: 1) isolate Gallant traffic in eu-west1 to stop routing to degraded nodes (traffic drain), 2) redirect new sessions to warm us-east1 pool, 3) coordinate DNS CNAME update for customer-facing host if TTL allows, 4) mitigation verification then incremental traffic cutover.

alex_soleng: starting traffic drain command now: `rdw-router weight-set --tenant gallant --region eu-west1 --weight 0.0 --shard default --reason \"incident 2333333000 drain\"` — will keep connections for 30s grace.

release-bot: deploy blocked? No active rollout in eu-west1 for gallant. Noted.

oncall-sre: drain initiated at 2333333050. Watching connections.

kyle_infra: bringing warm pool to steady state in us-east1: `rdwctl pool scale dedicated-gpu-42-warm --replicas 6 --region us-east1` done. healthchecks passing at 2333333075.

sasha_neteng: routing update: set tenant routing preference to prefer us-east1 for new connections: `rdw-router route-update --tenant gallant --prefer-region us-east1 --mode gradual`

marta_pm: ops:liaison, customer asks if we will change their public hostname or we will NAT at our edge. They prefer we avoid touching their DNS if possible.

ops:liaison: customer-ops-gallant asks for option A (edge-level redirect) first. We should keep DNS changes as a fallback within their agreed runbook.

oncall-sre: agreed. we'll do edge-level routing: no DNS change unless edge fallback fails. Proceeding with weighted shift: 90% new sessions -> us-east1 over 10 minutes.

alex_soleng: kicking canary traffic: `rdw-router weight-increment --tenant gallant --from eu-west1 --to us-east1 --percent 10 --interval 60s` — first step done at 2333333105.

customer-ops-gallant: seeing reduced errors for a subset of requests. thank you. still about 10% errors overall.

oncall-sre: monitoring logs and tracing. any sign of data plane incompat (model version mismatch) on warm pool?

kyle_infra: warm pool is using model v2.3.1 which is compatible with Gallant's pinned model v2.3.1. KV caches primed. no version mismatch.

alex_soleng: noticed a few 502s from a proxy layer while connections rebalanced. applying small bump to proxy keepalive.

sasha_neteng: also reduced client-side SYN retries by tuning proxy settings. pushed `haproxy.keepalive=on` to edge

marta_pm: customer says their internal dashboard shows latency dropping for most regions. asking for ETA to full recovery.

oncall-sre: estimate: if no regressions, finish gradual cutover to 100% us-east1 for new sessions in ~10 minutes; then drain existing eu-west1 connections (up to 2 minutes grace) and confirm recovery. ETA ~12–15 minutes.

ops:liaison: customer requests a short post-incident note and whether any requests were lost. We'll collect logs and provide a summary.

release-bot: note: there is a pending infra maintenance in eu-west1 in 6 hours — unrelated but FYI.

oncall-sre: can network team confirm there are no regional BGP issues? sasha_neteng?

sasha_neteng: no BGP anomalies. traffic pattern indicates origin-side burst plus app-level resource pressure.

customer-ops-gallant: we did release a heavier ingestion batch at 2333332945 which likely contributed. apologies, we'll throttle if needed.

marta_pm: good to know. Ops: after recovery we'll propose a joint traffic shaping policy for peak windows.

kyle_infra: drain completion: eu-west1 weight is 0 for new sessions at 2333333185. active connections left: 14, closing gracefully.

oncall-sre: verifying telemetry: 5xx rate down from 28% -> 2.1% across Gallant endpoints. tail latency p95 from 1.6s -> 230ms. marking mitigated.

customer-ops-gallant: confirmed on our side too — errors down and order ingestion resumed. thx everyone.

oncall-sre: final steps: 1) keep warm pool in us-east1 until we confirm eu-west1 nodes healthy and redeployed; 2) schedule a full root cause auth + postmortem. tagging infra and eng-runtime.

kyle_infra: root cause preliminary: pod OOMs due to a memory regression in model serving library combined with traffic burst. Will roll back the library in eu-west1 and repro on canary.

marta_pm: i'll arrange postmortem and customer-facing summary. ops:liaison please coordinate SLAs and impact messaging.

ops:liaison: will draft message and circulate. thanks all. handoff to oncall-sre for monitoring for 1h then close.

oncall-sre: monitoring, will escalate if metrics re-spike. closing bridge in 10 min if stable. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident duration so far: ~3.3 minutes to mitigation. Incident ticket: INC-2333333000
